turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Meredith's frame is in the project folder, so I'll play her from it, not from my own sense of what a parent would say. One thing I'll keep out of the scene: if you ever step out and mean it, or something real comes up for you or anyone else, I'll answer you as myself.

Hale, I'll be direct. Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother. I have a client call at 4:40, so start talking.
Go on, Hale. Owen, the zero, what's the next sentence?
I have 140 students. I don't have time to be cross-examined by every parent with a law degree.
Then don't. You entered a zero on my son's essay and I found out from his phone in front of his class. Start there.
You don't get to talk to me like I'm on the stand.
I'm not on the stand, Hale. I'm asking you a question you haven't answered. Who decided the zero, and did anyone call me before it went into the gradebook?
